requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of disk-backed swap on node1 and leave it active.
requirements.summary: The baseline contained only /dev/vda3. Final observations show a fully allocated, single-extent /swapfile with 545,255,424 usable bytes, mode 0600, swapfile_t labeling, and active swap status.

requirements.requirement: Make the added swap active automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The fstab entry generated an active systemd swap unit. A bounded reboot changed the boot identity, after which /swapfile automatically returned active with SourcePath=/etc/fstab and the host reached a healthy running state.

requirements.requirement: Prefer the added swap over every existing swap area.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, /swapfile had priority 100 while the only pre-existing swap, /dev/vda3, had priority -2.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Lifecycle observations show RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 both before and after execution. The implementation used the already-installed util-linux and coreutils facilities; final package health remained successful.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has more than 512 MiB of active disk-backed swap at higher priority than its existing swap, and direct reboot evidence proves automatic recovery. The required provider-wide restart protocol is complete for the sole managed node and agrees with the fixed lifecycle boot identities. The operating-system release, kernel, access, security posture, listeners, and package health were preserved.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The protected fstab backup supported rollback; initial swap creation, activation, resizing, and clean recreation were directly connected corrective steps; the fstab change established persistence; and the transient reboot exercised the required boot behavior. The reboot unit left no detected residue. Final lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, no new listeners, healthy package management, and only expected boot-scoped temporary-file and process-ID changes. The ip_set warning was present before execution and was not executor-caused.
